title: AI Engineering
author: Carnegie Mellon University Software Engineering Institute
claim: AI engineering combines systems and software engineering with computer science and human-centered design; SEI identifies human-centered, scalable, and robust and secure pillars.
limitation: A broad institutional definition, not a universal occupational credential or a definition limited to foundation models.
access_note: Official overview read during research.

title: The Rise of the AI Engineer
author: Shawn Wang
claim: Describes an emerging application-engineering role around foundation models, while acknowledging overlap across model and application work.
limitation: Advocacy and historical framing; employment forecasts and salary examples were not used as current evidence.
access_note: Original essay read during research.

title: The Shift from Models to Compound AI Systems
author: Matei Zaharia, Omar Khattab, Lingjiao Chen, Jared Quincy Davis, Heather Miller, Chris Potts, James Zou, Michael Carbin, Jonathan Frankle, Naveen Rao, and Ali Ghodsi
claim: Defines compound systems as interacting models, retrieval, and tools; discusses system design and end-to-end optimization.
limitation: A research perspective rather than proof that complex architectures always outperform simple ones.
access_note: Substantial publisher-indexed text was retrieved; direct page fetches timed out. Do not imply full direct-page access.

title: AI Engineering book and other resources
author: Chip Huyen
claim: Describes foundation-model application engineering and states that the book is not a tutorial book; distinguishes its focus from traditional ML-system development.
limitation: Used for positioning and scope, not for reproducing the book's contents or validating market demand.
access_note: Author-maintained README read directly.

title: Machine Learning Crash Course prerequisites and prework
author: Google
claim: Does not require previous ML knowledge; expects programming and basic quantitative skills, and labels calculus optional for advanced topics.
limitation: Entry requirements establish accessibility, not sufficient professional competence or the optimal learning sequence.
access_note: Official prerequisite page read directly, including the dated update.

title: CS336 Language Modeling from Scratch
author: Tatsunori Hashimoto and Percy Liang, Stanford University
claim: Model construction requires deeper ML, mathematics, and systems prerequisites; assignments cover construction, data, scaling, optimization, and post-training.
limitation: A model-building specialization whose complete prerequisite burden should not be imposed on application-engineering beginners.
access_note: Current course overview, prerequisites, and assignment descriptions read directly; listed cloud prices are not used.

title: LLM Bootcamp
author: Full Stack Deep Learning
claim: Combines a working application with model foundations, prompting, augmented models, UX, and operations.
limitation: Supports lifecycle coverage and practical pedagogy; tooling and specific implementation details are historical.
access_note: Official curriculum page read directly.

title: Framing an ML problem
author: Google
claim: Separates ideal product outcome, model goal, outputs, and business success metrics.
limitation: Instructional examples simplify real-world decision contexts; the proposed support application is editorial work.
access_note: Official page reviewed during research.

title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
author: Anthropic engineering team
claim: Distinguishes tasks, trials, graders, transcripts, outcomes, and harnesses; recommends evaluating actual outcomes and calibrating model graders.
limitation: Experience-based guidance, not controlled proof of one universally effective evaluation procedure; benchmark headlines are not adopted.
access_note: Official article read, including outcome definitions, graders, repeated trials, and evaluation-maintenance sections.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
author: Lianmin Zheng and colleagues
kind: Original research, NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks
claim: Reports agreement with human preferences in studied settings and identifies position, verbosity, self-enhancement, and reasoning limitations.
limitation: Preference agreement is not correctness; performance must be revalidated for another domain, rubric, or model.
access_note: Original abstract, authorship, submission history, and venue metadata checked.

title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
author: Margaret Mitchell and colleagues
claim: Proposes documenting intended uses, evaluation procedures, and performance under relevant conditions and across groups.
limitation: Documentation promotes transparency but does not certify fitness or eliminate risks.
access_note: Original abstract and authorship retrieved.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
author: Patrick Lewis and colleagues
claim: Combines parametric model memory with retrieved non-parametric evidence for generation.
limitation: The original trained architecture differs from many contemporary application-level RAG pipelines; historical results are not present-day rankings.
access_note: Original abstract and publication metadata retrieved.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation or Long-Context LLMs? A Comprehensive Study and Hybrid Approach
author: Zhuowan Li, Cheng Li, Mingyang Zhang, Qiaozhu Mei, and Michael Bendersky
claim: Compares retrieval and long-context approaches; reports quality and cost tradeoffs within the studied models and tasks.
limitation: Does not establish a universal winner or current model economics.
access_note: Publisher abstract and paper metadata retrieved.

title: Long Context vs. RAG for LLMs: An Evaluation and Revisits
author: Xinze Li, Yixin Cao, Yubo Ma, and Aixin Sun
claim: Revisits evaluation design and reports differences by task and retrieval method, emphasizing context relevance.
limitation: Results are bounded by the datasets, model versions, and methods studied; the arXiv identifier should not be mistaken for the submission date.
access_note: Original abstract and submission history read directly.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
author: Nelson F. Liu and colleagues
claim: Finds position-sensitive use of information in tested long-context question answering and retrieval tasks.
limitation: Provides a failure class and evaluation method, not proof that all future models have an identical degradation curve.
access_note: Publisher abstract, authorship, and venue metadata retrieved.

title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
author: Anthropic Applied AI team
claim: Treats instructions, tools, external data, and history as managed context; discusses compaction and persistent notes.
limitation: Practical recommendations and explanatory intuitions should be evaluated on the target model and workload.
access_note: Official article read directly, including context definitions and long-horizon strategies.

title: Building effective agents
author: Anthropic
claim: Distinguishes predefined workflows from model-directed control and recommends increasing complexity only when needed.
limitation: Architecture patterns remain useful but named tools on the living page have changed since initial publication.
access_note: Official page read directly; visible notice says the tooling landscape has changed.

title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
author: Justin Young, Anthropic
claim: Describes incremental work, persistent progress artifacts, environment checks, and testing across context windows.
limitation: A coding-focused demonstration; generalization and optimal single-agent versus multi-agent architecture remain open.
access_note: Official article read, including failure modes, testing, and future-work limitations.

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
author: Anthropic engineering team
claim: Documents research delegation and its coordination, evaluation, reliability, and token-consumption tradeoffs.
limitation: Internal comparisons do not establish that delegation is best for all tasks or under equal resources.
access_note: Official architecture and benefits/limitations sections read directly.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
author: Edward J. Hu and colleagues
claim: Freezes pretrained weights and introduces trainable low-rank matrices to reduce the trainable parameter burden.
limitation: Does not imply adaptation is always necessary or that an adapter matches full fine-tuning on every task.
access_note: Original abstract and authorship checked.

title: MMMU-Pro: A More Robust Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding Benchmark
author: Xiang Yue and colleagues
claim: Strengthens multimodal evaluation by removing text-only shortcuts and testing questions embedded in images.
limitation: A benchmark-design lesson, not evidence for universal current multimodal capability or application accuracy.
access_note: Original abstract, revision history, and venue metadata read directly.

title: OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 2026
author: OWASP GenAI Security Project
claim: Provides application threat scenarios and mitigations covering injection, disclosure, authority, resource consumption, and other risks.
limitation: A prioritization aid rather than universal risk prevalence or a compliance certification. Publication landing pages differ by one day, so month is used.
access_note: Official landing page dated August 3 opened; linked 122-page PDF accessible; project preface examined in research lane.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
author: Chloe Autio, Reva Schwartz, Jesse Dunietz, Shomik Jain, Martin Stanley, Elham Tabassi, Patrick Hall, and Kamie Roberts
kind: Voluntary government risk-management guidance, NIST AI 600-1
claim: Addresses context-dependent risks across the lifecycle, including privacy, confabulation, harmful bias, human configuration, and component integration.
limitation: Voluntary guidance; use does not establish legal compliance or eliminate harm. Historical executive-order context is not treated as current law.
access_note: Official publication page and 64-page PDF opened; introduction and risk categories read.

title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction
author: Saleema Amershi and colleagues
claim: Proposes 18 interaction guidelines and evaluates relevance through multiple rounds, including 49 practitioners examining 20 products.
limitation: Predates current foundation-model agents and does not prove every proposed interface improves outcomes.
access_note: Official publication abstract and study summary retrieved.

title: A postmortem of three recent issues
author: Sam McAllister, Anthropic
claim: Infrastructure and routing changes produced behavioral regressions that existing evaluations missed; remediation included production-quality evaluation and better diagnostics.
limitation: Not independently audited and not representative failure-frequency evidence; protects the distinction between model and application/provider failures.
access_note: Official detection, remediation, technical-cause, and privacy discussion read directly.

title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
author: Lingjiao Chen, Matei Zaharia, and James Zou
claim: Explores prompt adaptation, approximation, and cascades to improve task-specific quality/cost tradeoffs.
limitation: Historical prices, models, and maximum reported savings are not forecasts for present systems.
access_note: Original abstract and submission metadata read directly.
